memory_candidates.content: In this repo's merge.lua generate_claudemd(), only the per-extension claudemd fragments are right-trimmed (fragment:gsub("%s+$", "")) before joining with "\n\n" -- the prepended core header template is inserted UNTRIMMED. claudemd-header.md ends in two raw newlines, so a byte-exact bash replication of the assembly must either materialize the document in a scratch file and measure it with wc -c, or account for this header/fragment trim asymmetry explicitly in any hand-rolled arithmetic. The materialize-and-measure route is far less error-prone.

Bash gotcha: `local a="$1" b="$a"` (two assignments in one local statement, the second referencing the first) silently leaves b empty -- bash does not make a's newly-assigned value visible to a later assignment within the same local statement. Split into two separate `local` statements to fix. Easy to miss because the bug is silent (no error), and it manifested as an ERE regex collapsing to '^$' that matched nothing.

Glob-to-ERE translation for paths: frontmatter matching (specs/**/*, .claude/**/*, **/*.lean style globs): bash's own [[ str == pattern ]] treats ** as a plain * (does not cross /) even with shopt -s globstar, so it silently fails to match nested paths. Correct approach: hand-translate the glob to a POSIX ERE (escape regex metachars except */?, then **/  -> (.*/)? , remaining ** -> .*, * -> [^/]*, ? -> [^/] , anchor ^...$) and match with [[ str =~ ere ]].
